title: Smoke and fire on the hill
notes: Smoke is absent from red-hot iron, which has fire, so presence in sapaksa is partial.

title: Sound is impermanent because produced
notes: Mimamsakas dispute the thesis (sound is eternal). That dispute is not modelled here.

title: Sound is eternal because audible
notes: Dignaga's standard example of a reason that is too specific (asadharana): audibility belongs to sound alone.

title: Sound is impermanent because knowable
notes: A reason too broad to discriminate (sadharana).

title: Sound is eternal because produced
notes: The reason proves the opposite of the thesis (viruddha).

title: The pot is nameable because knowable
notes: Nyaya's standard kevalanvayi example (nothing is unnameable). Jain annotation left empty: anekanta and avaktavya may block the premise. Needs a scholar's reading.

title: Earth differs from the other elements because it has smell
thesis: Earth differs from the other elements
notes: Nyaya's standard kevalavyatireki example, valid by negative concomitance alone.

title: Rohini will rise because Krttika has risen
notes: Used in the Jain case that pakshadharmata is not required. Buddhist and Nyaya replies may redefine the subject; the engines show only the structural verdicts.

title: He is dark because he is her son
notes: Classically cited as a case where the three characteristics hold yet the inference fails, with a hidden factor (the mother's diet) as the upadhi. Check the exact formulation in the sources before citing.

title: The pot is momentary because it exists
notes: Base facts are the Buddhist stipulation. Nyaya and Jain ontologies admit enduring things that exist, so the same inference fails there. This case isolates ontology from logic. Follows the Dharmakirtian sattvanumana (momentariness from existence); passage pointer: TODO, see docs/CITATIONS.md row 8.

title: The hill has smoke because it has fire
notes: Standard upadhi illustration: contact with wet fuel conditions the smoke. Red-hot iron has fire without smoke.

title: There is no pot on the table
thesis: There is no pot on this table
reason: because a pot, if present, would be seen, and is not seen
notes: Dharmakirti's non-perception reason. Nyaya treats the same cognition as perception of absence. The condition that the object would be seen if present is attested as a commentator's point (Nagatomi 1957, pp. 124 to 125); the PV 1 / PVSV pointer is still needed. Passage pointer: TODO.

title: Fire is not hot because it is a substance
notes: Standard badhita illustration: the thesis is refuted by touch, so the reason is blocked.
